newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices firm at week's sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices firm at week's sales.

text.p: Australian wool prices rose by six percent across the board at sales this week in Sydney and Geelong, pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety said.
The eastern market indicator rose 33 cents to 617 cents a kg clean, reaching the highest level for the season.
In the two weeks of selling after the mid-season break the eastern market indicator has gained 50 cents.
A total of 53,462 bales was offered, the lowest weekly offering for the season to date. The trade bought 96.6 percent, with a pass-in rate of 3.4 percent.
Wool International said trade competition was led by Japanese and Chinese buyers with good support from Western European buyers and most sectors of the trade.

"While there is good demand for the best quality wools on offer, exporters reported that the overall makret sentiment is being driven by the relatively small quantities rostered for sale in January," it said.
The other significant factor at present is the continued strength of buying by the largest auction buying firm, Itochu Australia Ltd, The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
Wool International said its stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,900,596 bales as of January 16.
In the futures market, a total of 215 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended January 16.
The February contract rose 24 cents to 727 cents a kg clean.
Open interest increased by 17 contracts to close at 882.
Sales next week are in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with 74,200 bales rostered for sale.
